full_judgment:
Short facts leading to this application are that the Respondent No. 1 (hereinafter called the respondent) was the acting Head Cashier  of the then National Bank of Pakistan posted at Ajrnirigonj, Sylhet and he was placed under suspension on 18.7.66 on account of short-age in cash to the extent of Tk. 19,050.12 paisa and the suspension order has been annexed to the petition as Annexure 'A'. The respondent sent a representation to the petitioner Bark on 30.4.67 requesting them to pay subsistence allowance which was not being paid to him, a copy of the said letter has been marked as Annexure 'B'. The petitioners in reply in-formed the respondent that he was not entitled to the subsistence allowance since he did not stay in the head quarter as required under the rules. The said reply has been annexed to the petition as Annexure 'C'. Thereafter the respondent submitted another representation to the petitioner purporting to be a grievance petition under section 25 of the Employment and Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 (hereinafter called the Act) on 7. 10. 69, a copy of which was annexed to the petition as Annexure 'D' and a reply to which was also sent by the petitioner rejecting the said grievance petition, by a letter dated 25. 10. 69, a copy of which was annexed to the petition as Annexure `E'. In the meanwhile, a criminal case was started by the police against the respondent which was pending and the petitioners also filed a civil suit for recovery of the bank dues against the respondent as well as the insurance company. Thereafter the respondent filed a complaint case before the First Labour Court at Dacca under section 25 of the said Act praying for reinstatement and for subsistence allowance at the rate of half of his average pay. The petitioners contended the said case by filing written statement wherein they denied the materials allegations made in the petition and further asserted that the case was barred by limitation. 

 3. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has urged two grounds in support of the rule. He has firstly argued that the application under section 25 of the Act was clearly barred by limitation and secondly, he has argued that the respondent was not a 'worker' within the meaning of section 2(v) of the Act. 

 8. It appears that although the petitioners in their written statement before the court below raised an objection regarding limitation, the Labour Court neither considered the point nor came to any finding. Mr. Hossain has argued that even if the letter dated 30.4.67 (annexure 'B') is construed as a grievance petition as required under section 25 of the Act, the reply having been given on 1.6.67, and the respondent having filed the case after about 2-1/2 years from the date of the decision, the case was hopelessly barred under the law. 

 10. With regard to the next submission of Mr. Hossain that the respondent was not a 'worker' within the meaning of section 2(v) of the Act, it appears that the learned Labour Court found that the respondent was a worker'. Since this point was not disputed by the petitioner before the Court below and having regard to our findings above on the question of limitation, we do not think any decision is called for in the instant case.
